children: MDxHealth suspended its full-year outlook, after preliminary revenue fell short of the company's expectations during the latest quarter.
The company said Thursday it expects to report third-quarter revenue from continuing operations of about $22.7 million, missing the $28.8 million that analysts polled by FactSet expected.
Chief Executive Michael McGarrity attributed the shortcoming to unexpected turnover across the company's sales force, which was aggressively targeted by recruiters during the period.

"While we have a disciplined process which has served as the foundation of our forecast accuracy over the past three years, that process was clearly disrupted by this recent impact on our sales force," he said.

Looking ahead, MDxHealth no longer expects revenue of $110 million to $115 million for the year. The company said it plans to provide additional information when it reports its full third-quarter results next month.
Shares fell 8.9%, to 55 cents, in after-hours trading.
